Specify the hazard model of an event process

Source: R/hazard-model.R
hazard_model.Rd

Describes how fit_initial() models the hazard of one event process. A plain formula such as death ~ L0 + z in models is short for hazard_model(death ~ L0 + z); use hazard_model() to also restrict when an individual is at risk of the process, or to change how it is fitted.

Usage

hazard_model(formula, limit = NULL, at_risk = NULL, fit = c("cox", "hal"))

Arguments

formula

A two-sided formula. The left-hand side names the process, matching its name in the event column of the data, and the right-hand side gives the covariates of its hazard, as in a survival::coxph() formula. Other processes can be used as covariates by name, giving their number of events so far.

limit

Optional positive integer. Maximum number of events of the process per individual: individuals are only at risk while they have had fewer than limit events. limit = 1 is an event that can happen at most once, as sim_process(limit = 1) in simevent.

at_risk

Optional one-sided formula, such as ~ z == 0, of a condition on the processes (their number of events so far). Individuals are only at risk of the process while it holds. Combined with limit if both are given.

fit

How the hazard is fitted: "cox" (default), a Cox model, or "hal", the highly adaptive lasso (experimental, see fit_initial()).

Value

An object of class hazard_model.

Examples

# A plain formula in fit_initial()'s `models` is short for
# hazard_model(formula):
hazard_model(death ~ L0 + z)
#> Hazard model: death ~ L0 + z

# An illness that can happen at most once:
hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1)
#> Hazard model: z ~ L0
#>   limit: 1

# A relapse that can happen at most twice, and only before death of
# another cause, w:
hazard_model(relapse ~ L0, limit = 2, at_risk = ~ w == 0)
#> Hazard model: relapse ~ L0
#>   limit: 2
#>   at risk while: w == 0

# Death depending on having had two or more relapses. As in any R model
# formula, wrap arithmetic and comparisons in I():
hazard_model(death ~ L0 + I(relapse >= 2))
#> Hazard model: death ~ L0 + I(relapse >= 2)

# Use them in fit_initial(), mixed with plain formulas:
fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  models = list(
    hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),
    death ~ L0 + z,
    censoring ~ L0
  ),
  tau = 1
)
fit$processes
#>         name     type          model at_risk
#>       <char>   <char>         <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0    TRUE
#> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + z   FALSE
#> 3: censoring terminal censoring ~ L0   FALSE
